subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should OpenClaw make memorySearch.sync.intervalMinutes default-on as the stale-watcher safety net, or keep periodic memory sync opt-in and solve watcher failure through a narrower health/doctor path?
rationale: The source-level bug is real, but changing the unconfigured interval default affects existing users' background filesystem scans and possible indexing/provider work, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive product direction.

options.title: Accept default-on fallback after repair
options.body: Proceed with the linked PR direction after scoping dirty marking correctly, preserving intervalMinutes: 0 as the explicit opt-out, and documenting upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep periodic sync opt-in
options.body: Leave the default at 0 and require a narrower watcher-health warning, doctor recommendation, or setup guidance instead of automatic background sync.

options.title: Pause until live outage proof
options.body: Hold the default change until maintainers get a live long-running gateway/chokidar outage proof that justifies the upgrade behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept default-on fallback after repair
recommendation.body: Proceed with the linked PR direction after scoping dirty marking correctly, preserving intervalMinutes: 0 as the explicit opt-out, and documenting upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger introduced memory vector search and moved the memory engine into the plugin boundary, making him the strongest available owner for the default/fallback direction.
